(1) Each of V1-V6 is really closed in the text: DT-2d (every SEP row's «was» text equals the sample value at the same path in both tenants, ru kk en, word for word; rows with a check code skipped) and its mutant MU29 — apply MU29 to your own sketch of the data and confirm the check accepts it, so that only the test can catch it; the pin of engine.js is gone from DT-6b and table 8.3, and no other place still pins it; MU19 attribution (apply it); I1-I4 shown as answered by decisions/0086; E1 comparison rule (absent field, name.en literal) is unambiguous and true for the sample (run it on the sample module with a substituted window); DT-4b fold rule and MU30.
(2) Consistency after the rework: count the DT rows and MU rows yourself and compare with every place that states a count (summary, 6.x, 8.x, 13.x, the facts list); the criterion-to-test table covers criteria 1-7; no criterion is left to RELEASE-VALIDATOR only except the run-relative git diff command of criterion 6, which is allowed.
(3) The new DT-6b literals (engine results for the six OLD answer sets, ru kk en identical): reproduce them on a fresh clone of the tag base/DEMO070-20261027-01 in the session scratchpad folder named in the launching message, using the existing engine and the old demo answers.
(4) Repeat on your own sketch whatever else you consider risky after the rework (the full `npm run check` once with the four data files and a README paragraph placed in the copy, as in pass 1, must stay green); apply at least five more mutants of the design's list at random and two mutants of your own that are not in the list, and confirm each has a named test in the design that would catch it.
(5) No machine paths and no project names in the design or your handoff (say "the traces list"); the questions for ORCH: none open.
Verdict PASS or FAIL; only a High or Medium finding makes FAIL; Low findings go to the follow-up list. Change only your handoff. No commits, no git checkout/reset/stash/clean. 16 GB RAM computer: single commands, one run at a time.
